Andromeda design rulebook

Status: approved 2026-11-02. Built on "The Lens" (.agent/mockups/language.html). docs/design/rulebook.html is the one page to read: these chapters with live, interruptible demos and the deviation map (build: python3 docs/design/build_rulebook.py). This book is the only design source. A value that is not in this book, or not derived by one of its rules, is a bug. protocol/design-tokens.toml holds the same values as data; when the two differ, this book wins and the TOML is fixed.

0. How to use this book

  • Every size, gap, padding and radius comes from a scale (§2) or from a derivation rule (§2.2 R1-R9). Each component table in §6 and §9 names the rule next to each value. A reviewer checks a surface against the table, not against a screenshot.
  • Values are logical pixels at ui_scale 1. The toolkit multiplies by the scale and snaps edges to device pixels once, at layout. Never snap a size on its own: snap both edges, so a gap stays equal at 1.25 and 1.5.
  • corner_radius_scale multiplies every radius except capsules and circles; concentric radii are recomputed after the multiply (R7), never scaled separately.
  • A new component first gets an anatomy table here. Code follows the table.

1. Principles

  1. Glass over your wallpaper, solid where you read. Chrome floats as glass; windows and long text sit on solid planes.
  2. One selection object. The lens marks "you are here" in every component. Never an accent-filled pill.
  3. Accent means on. Accent colours on-states, the focus ring and the selected icon only. A screen at rest is nearly colourless.
  4. Things come from somewhere. A surface grows out of the thing you touched and returns there when it closes. Nothing appears from nowhere and nothing wipes in from a screen edge.
  5. One object, one motion. A shape moves on one spring: bounds, radius, shadow, blur and input together. Content inside it follows the shape; it never runs its own clock.
  6. Every value is designed. Sizes come from scales and rules. Nothing is nudged by a pixel to look right; if it looks wrong, the rule is wrong and gets fixed here.
  7. Fast to use, calm to look at. Motion confirms an action and shows where things went; it never makes the user wait. Input is accepted on the first frame of every animation.

2. Space, size and shape

2.1 Scales

Scale Values (px)
Space 2 (inside controls only), 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64
Control height 24 small, 32 regular, 40 large, 48 extra large (touch)
Row height 32 compact one-line, 40 one-line, 48 compact two-line, 56 two-line
Symbol size 12 inline, 16 standard, 20 large; 32, 48 in empty states
App icon size 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128
Radius 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, capsule (height / 2), circle
Hairline 0.5 (glass stroke), 1 (separator); device-pixel exact

2.2 Derivation rules

R1 Grid. Every position, size, padding, gap and radius is a multiple of 4. A 2 px step is allowed only inside a control of height 32 or less (segmented inset, toggle knob inset). Type sizes and hairlines are exempt; line heights are not (§3).

R2 Height from content. A container's height is its content height plus two paddings. Only controls and rows take a fixed height from §2.1; their vertical padding follows: (height - line height) / 2. Example: row 40 with a 16 px line: padding 12. Two-line row 56: 16 + 16 lines, padding 12.

R3 Proximity ladder. Inside a group the gap is 4 or 8. Between groups the gap is at least twice the gap inside them. A container's padding is at least its largest inside gap. Lines of one text block have gap 0 (the line heights space them).

R4 Symbol to label. A 12 or 16 symbol has gap 8 to its label; a 20 or larger symbol, or a round icon, has gap 12.

R5 End caps. In a capsule, a symbol at the end sits concentric with the cap: inset = (height - symbol) / 2. Text at the end of a capsule has inset = height x 3/8, rounded to 4 (24 -> 8, 32 -> 12, 40 -> 16, 56 -> 20). In a rounded rectangle, text inset is 12 at height 32 or more and 8 below that. A leading symbol in a rounded rectangle has inset = (height - symbol) / 2 rounded up to the 4 grid, at most 12 (28 -> 8, 32 -> 8, 40 -> 12). A key cap or chip at the end of a field keeps one inset on its top, bottom and end: (height - cap) / 2 (32 field, 20 cap -> 6).

R6 One edge. Inside a container, text starts on one vertical line. A section header, a row label and a footnote of the same group share that line. In a list, a row with a leading symbol, avatar or app icon indents its text past it (the separator indents with it); every row without one stays on the edge.

R7 Concentric radius. A shape inside another shape, at padding p from it, has radius = outer radius - p. Choose p so the result lands on the radius scale. Below 4 the result is 4. Capsules and circles stay capsules and circles. The focus ring is concentric outward: ring radius = shape radius + ring offset. Corners are continuous: superellipse with smoothing 0.6 (docs/design-system.md rule 14), the same formula in the shell, the compositor mask and the CSS. A corner too small to grow falls back toward a circular arc.

R8 Chrome gap. Floating chrome keeps 8 from the screen edge and from other chrome: bar islands, the dock, sheets under their island, banners, tiled windows (window to window and window to screen or bar). One number: 8.

R9 Optical corrections are listed, nowhere else. Allowed: a play triangle moves 1 px toward its open side; a battery symbol (wider than tall) centres on its body, not its tip; a glyph in a circle under 24 uses size 12.

2.3 Hit targets

Pointer: 24 x 24 minimum, invisible hit area extends a smaller visual to 24. Touch mode (tablet, touch input seen): 40 minimum, rows grow to 48 / 56 and controls to 40. Targets never overlap; a gap of 4 or more splits them.

3. Type

Inter (variable), tabular figures wherever a number changes (clock, percent, time, counts), cv11 single-storey a off. Line heights are multiples of 4. Tracking follows Inter's dynamic metrics: tracking(em) = -0.0223 + 0.185 x e^(-0.1745 x size).

Style Size / line Weight Tracking Use
caption 11 / 16 500 +0.5 % badges, keycaps, group headers in sidebars, timestamps
footnote 12 / 16 400 0 secondary lines, section headers (600), tooltips, field help
body 13 / 16 400 -0.3 % every one-line UI label; paragraphs use 13 / 20
headline 13 / 16 600 -0.3 % tile titles, row emphasis, window titles, the clock in the bar
title-3 15 / 20 600 -0.9 % dialog and alert titles, empty-state titles
title-2 17 / 24 600 -1.3 % page titles in app headers
title-1 22 / 28 600 -1.8 % large page titles, launcher section titles
large 28 / 32 600 -2.1 % onboarding, big numbers in widgets
display 34 / 40 500 -2.2 % lock-screen date line, OSD big values
hero 80 / 80 300 -2.2 % lock-screen clock only
  • Three weights only: 400, 500, 600 (300 for hero). No 700.
  • On glass, +100 weight for body and footnote (400 -> 500): text over blur needs the extra stem.
  • One line: ellipsis at the end; never shrink type to fit. Two lines maximum in rows and banners; then ellipsis.
  • Text size setting (S / M / L / XL = 0.92 / 1 / 1.15 / 1.3) scales sizes, rounds line heights up to the 4 grid, and containers grow by R2. Chrome heights (islands, dock) do not grow above L; their text truncates instead.

4. Colour

4.1 Roles

Labels and fills are black (light) or white (dark) at an opacity, so they work on any plane and on glass.

Role Light Dark Use
label_1 #141418 92 % #f4f4f6 92 % primary text and symbols
label_2 #141418 62 % #f4f4f6 62 % secondary text (>= 4.5:1 on every plane)
label_3 #141418 38 % #f4f4f6 38 % placeholders, disabled-looking hints, group headers; never essential text
fill_1 black 4 % white 6 % rest fill of tiles and tracks on glass, hover of a bare row
fill_2 black 8 % white 10 % hover of a fill_1 item, control tracks, round icon off
fill_3 black 12 % white 16 % hover of a fill_2 item, pressed of a fill_1 item
separator black 8 % white 8 % 1 px lines in lists and menus
stroke black 7 % white 8 % 0.5 px outline of glass and cards
edge white 75 % white 12 % 0.5 px inner top highlight of glass
accent #5147e5 #6159f5 on-state fills, focus ring; white glyphs and text on it (6.2:1 / 4.9:1)
accent_text #5147e5 #8c85ff accent symbols and text on planes (6.2:1 / 5.8:1)
danger #d93025 #d93025 destructive fills and the dock badge; white text on it (4.8:1)
danger_text #d93025 #ff6b5e error symbols and text, destructive menu items (4.8:1 / 6.3:1)
warning #b45309 #f5a524 low battery, risky settings
success #1a7f37 #3fb950 done, connected-and-verified

Fill ladder. Hover moves an item one step up the ladder (none -> fill_1 -> fill_2 -> fill_3); pressed moves two. There is no other hover colour.

Accent rule. Accent fills: a toggle that is on, a slider fill in a window, an active round icon, a primary button, a checked box or radio, the focus ring, the selected icon inside the lens. Accent never fills a selection, a hovered item, a header, a badge count or a decoration.

4.2 Contrast (computed, WCAG 2)

label_1 18.4:1 light card, 13.7:1 dark card. label_2 5.2:1 light card, 4.9:1 light plane, 6.2:1 dark card. label_3 2.4:1 / 3.2:1 (decorative only). accent text 6.2:1 / 5.8:1. Over glass the tint rule in §5.3 keeps label_2 at 4.5:1 or more.

4 · Colour

Roles, not colours

Hover moves one step up the fill ladder (none → fill_1 → fill_2 → fill_3). Accent fills only on-states, the focus ring and the lens symbol.

5. Material and depth

5.1 Planes

Plane Material Elevation Members
wallpaper the image - the only large colour field
float regular glass E2 bar islands, dock, center island at rest
over thick glass E3 sheets (control center, launcher, notification center), menus, popovers, banners, tooltips, OSD
window solid E4 active, E3 inactive app windows, Settings, dialogs (dialogs: E4 always)
in-window solid E0 (stroke only) cards, fields, tables inside windows

Glass never sits under text you read for longer than a glance. A window sidebar may use thick glass (short labels).

5.2 Glass recipes

Material Light tint Dark tint Blur
regular white 62 % #1c1c20 70 % dual Kawase 3 passes, radius 6, noise 0.02
thick white 76 % #202024 84 % same
light recipe saturation 1.8, brightness 1.05, contrast 1.0 -
dark recipe - saturation 1.6, brightness 0.95, contrast 0.95

Every glass shape draws: tint, 0.5 px stroke outline, 0.5 px edge highlight on the inner top edge, then its shadow. The compositor draws blur and shadow; the client draws tint and content.

5.3 Readable glass

Each tint rises toward the next material until label_2 over the sampled backdrop reaches 4.5:1: regular toward thick, thick toward its solid fallback. Over a calm wallpaper nothing changes; over a busy or black window the float plane reaches thick and the over plane nears solid (thick light glass over pure black gives label_2 only 4.1:1 without this rule). Reduce transparency replaces every material with its solid fallback (light #f2f2f6 / #f8f8fa, dark #222226 / #28282c).

5.4 Elevation

Two shadows per level: a key shadow (y offset = 3/8 of blur) and a contact shadow. Shadow colour: light rgb(20,20,40), dark black.

Level Key (y / blur / opacity light, dark) Contact Members
E0 none 0.5 px stroke cards and fields in windows
E1 1 / 2 / 10 %, 30 % 0.5 px ring 7 % the lens, toggle knob, slider knob
E2 6 / 16 / 12 %, 30 % 1 / 4 / 8 %, 20 % float plane
E3 12 / 32 / 16 %, 40 % 2 / 8 / 8 %, 24 % over plane, inactive windows
E4 24 / 64 / 22 %, 50 % 2 / 8 / 10 %, 30 % active window, dialogs

Elevation is an animatable property: a morph from E2 to E3 interpolates the shadow on the shape's spring (§7).

6. The lens (selection object)

The lens is a lifted pane: fill white 92 % (light) or white 14 % (dark), E1 shadow, dark: 0.5 px inner top edge white 18 %. Inside the lens, text goes to label_1 and weight 600; the symbol takes accent_text.

Where Lens shape Inset in its track
sidebar row rect r 8 fills the row
segmented control capsule 2
workspace cells in the left island capsule 24 4 (concentric in the 32 island)
tab strip rect r 8 4
dock (focused app) rect r 20, 56 x 56 4 (concentric in the dock, r 24)
menu (current item) rect r 8 4 (concentric in the menu, r 12)
grouped list in a window rect r 8 4 (concentric in the card, r 12)
launcher grid (current cell) rect r 16 cell bounds

States of any selectable item:

State Look
rest no fill
hover fill ladder one step (wash)
pressed lens at the P2 press scale, fill dimmed 3 %
selected lens
selected + keyboard focus lens + focus ring (2 px accent, 2 px gap, concentric)
disabled whole item 38 % opacity, no hover

The lens never fades between items: it travels (§7.6 P1). One track has exactly one lens.

6 · The lens

One selection object, every state

7. Motion

7.1 Rules

  1. Springs only. Every animation is a spring with a response d (s) and bounce b. No duration-and-easing animations, except continuous loops (spinners, indeterminate bars, shimmer), which are linear, and transitions whose length the user sets (wallpaper change, lock-screen shader).
  2. Spatial may bounce; effects never do. Position, size, clip, radius, scale and elevation use spatial springs. Opacity, colour and blur use effect springs (bounce 0).
  3. Bounce where momentum arrives. Opening, morphing, a release after a press and a lens arrival bounce. Closing, fading and page changes do not.
  4. Exits are faster than entries (close 0.28 s against open 0.42 s) and never stagger.
  5. Retarget, never restart. A new target keeps the current value and velocity. No animation queues behind another. Reversing mid-flight turns the same spring around.
  6. Gate on progress, not on time. "Content fades in after 35 %" means 35 % of the shape's travel, so the choreography holds when a gesture drives the shape or a retarget changes its speed.
  7. One driver per shape. The compositor owns a surface's bounds, clip, radius, elevation and opacity (dsk_surface_v1). The client owns the content inside and follows the compositor's clock (started).
  8. Input never waits. A surface takes input on its first frame; a press during a close reopens it.
  9. Idle is zero frames. A spring stops at |x - target| < threshold and |v| < 62.5 x threshold, sets the exact target and stops asking for frames. Thresholds: 0.5 px, scale 0.002, opacity 1/256.

7.2 Spring set

k = (2 pi / d)^2, damping ratio z = 1 - b, mass 1. Settle = time until the error stays under 0.5 %.

Spring d b k z Settle Overshoot Use
snap 0.26 0.15 584 0.85 280 ms 0.6 % lens leading edge, toggle knob, checkbox, small control positions
trail 0.34 0.20 342 0.80 390 ms 1.5 % lens trailing edge (makes the stretch)
move 0.35 0.10 322 0.90 310 ms 0.1 % reflow: list insert/remove/reorder, banner stack, window tiling
open 0.42 0.22 224 0.78 480 ms 1.9 % a surface grows from its source
close 0.28 0 504 1.00 330 ms 0 a surface returns to its source, dismissals
morph 0.46 0.25 187 0.75 530 ms 2.8 % center island expands (media, banner, OSD, live activity)
collapse 0.32 0.10 386 0.90 280 ms 0.1 % center island returns to rest
page 0.32 0.05 386 0.95 330 ms 0 + velocity pages, workspaces, gesture release (carries finger velocity)
press 0.12 0 2742 1.00 140 ms 0 press down
release 0.32 0.25 386 0.75 370 ms 2.8 % release after a press
fade 0.16 0 1542 1.00 190 ms 0 opacity, colour, blur in
fade_out 0.10 0 3948 1.00 120 ms 0 opacity, colour, blur out

Overshoot is a fraction of the travel: a 360 px sheet that opens with 1.9 % passes its rest size by 7 px, enough to feel alive, small enough not to read as a wobble.

7.3 The six motion verbs

Every transition is one of these. A transition that is not one of them is not allowed.

Verb What moves Springs
Grow a surface from its source rect to its own rect (shared element) open; content fade
Return the reverse of Grow, into the source close; content fade_out
Morph one shape changes size and content in place (center island) morph / collapse; faces cross
Slide peers replace each other on one axis (pages, workspaces, tabs' content) page
Travel the lens moves between items snap (leading edge) + trail (trailing edge)
Press an item gives under the pointer and springs back press / release

Fade alone is allowed only for: tooltips, hover washes, content swaps inside a frame that does not move, and reduced motion.

7.4 Choreography

  • The shape leads, content follows. Content opacity starts on fade when the shape passes 35 % of its travel. Until it settles, content scales with the shape (uniform fit to the current bounds); then it shows at 1:1.
  • Exits overlap. On Return, content fade_out and the shape's close start on the same frame. Nothing waits.
  • Cross the faces. In a Morph the outgoing face fades out (fade_out), scales to 0.92 and blurs to 8 px; the incoming face fades in from 50 % of travel, from scale 0.92 and blur 8 px to 1 and 0. Both stay inside the clip.
  • Stagger entries only. Children of a growing surface start 16 ms apart; the sixth starts at 80 ms and the rest start with it. This is the one time offset in the system. Exits never stagger.
  • Source hand-off. A source that becomes the surface (the center island, a dock icon that opens a window, a banner that opens the notification center) hides its face on the frame Grow starts: the growing shape IS the source. On Return its face fades back in from 70 % of the close travel. A source that stays in place (a bar island, a button) keeps its face and shows its open state (tint regular -> thick on fade) while its surface is open.
  • Keep relative placement. An element that exists in both states (an app icon in the island and in the banner) moves on the shape's spring from its old place to its new place; it does not fade out and in.
  • Depth recedes. When an over-plane surface opens, nothing behind it scales or dims, except a modal dialog (scrim 20 % black light, 40 % dark on fade).

7.5 Origin and return

Every transient surface records its source rect when it opens: the island, the button, the dock icon, the pointer point (context menu), the notification (for an opened app). It closes into the current rect of that source. If the source is gone, it closes into the source's last rect with scale 0.92 and fade_out. Keyboard-opened surfaces use the focused control as the source; global shortcuts use the island that owns the surface.

7.6 Patterns

# Pattern Trigger Path and springs
P1 Lens travel select another item leading edge on snap, trailing edge on trail: the lens stretches toward the target (up to the gap it crosses) and settles; text weight and symbol colour cross on fade at 50 %
P2 Press pointer down / up scale 0.96 (items up to 96 px), 0.98 (up to 240 px), none above (fill ladder step instead); press down, release up
P3 Hover pointer enters / leaves fill one ladder step: in on fade_out (quick), out on fade (slower), so a quick pass does not flicker
P4 Toggle click / Space knob travels on snap; while pressed the knob widens by 6 px toward the travel side; track colour on fade
P5 Sheet from island click island, drag, shortcut Grow: clip x, y, w, h, radius (16 -> 28), elevation (E2 -> E3) on open; tint regular -> thick on fade; the island-facing edge stays fixed; tiles stagger in
P6 Sheet follows the finger drag down from the island clip tracks the pointer 1:1 with 8 px slop; release projects the end point and settles on page with the finger's velocity (§7.7)
P7 Center island morph media, banner, OSD, call Morph on morph; back to rest on collapse; elevation E2 -> E3 -> E2 on the same spring; faces cross (§7.4)
P8 Banner stack second banner arrives the old banner moves down 8 and scales to 0.96 on move; the new one Morphs out of the island; three visible, older ones stack behind
P9 Banner dismiss swipe up / right, timeout swipe: follows the finger, release on page with velocity, then fade_out; timeout: Return into the island on close
P10 Menu / popover click a button, right-click Grow from the anchor corner (button edge or pointer point): scale 0.92 -> 1 on open with opacity on fade; Return: opacity on fade_out with scale 1 -> 0.96 toward the anchor on close
P11 Dialog an app or the shell asks from the triggering control if known, else the parent window centre: scale 0.96 -> 1 on open, opacity fade, scrim fade; Return on close
P12 Page / workspace swipe, keys, click Slide: incoming and outgoing move together 1:1 with a 32 px gap; deeper level: outgoing moves 30 % and dims 10 % (parallax); back reverses
P13 List change insert, remove, reorder remaining items reflow on move; an inserted row grows its height from 0 on move with content fade from 35 %; a removed row fades out, then its height closes on move
P14 Content swap a value or a text changes number: old digits move up 8 px and fade_out, new digits come from 8 px below on fade (per changed digit); symbol: crossfade with scale 0.8 -> 1 on snap
P15 Window open launch from dock / launcher Grow from the launching icon rect (snapshot scaled until the first client commit), open; from a shortcut: scale 0.94 -> 1 from the window centre
P16 Window close / minimize close button, minimize close: scale 1 -> 0.96 and fade_out; minimize: Return into the dock icon on close
P17 Window tile / maximize drag to edge, key the frame moves on move; content shows the scaled snapshot until the client commits the new size, then cross on fade
P18 Overview gesture, key each window moves from its place to its overview slot on page (gesture-driven); the wallpaper dims 20 % on fade
P19 Launcher click dock launcher / Super Grow out of the dock launcher button (or the left island when the dock is off)
P20 Lock / unlock lock, auth success lock: the screen dims and blurs on fade, the clock Grows from the center island; unlock: the clock Returns into the center island, blur fades out
P21 Loading content not ready after 200 ms skeleton blocks shimmer (1.4 s linear loop); spinner only for an unknown-size action; once shown, it stays 400 ms or more

7.7 Gestures

  • Slop: 8 px before a drag claims an axis. Touchpad swipes: 3 fingers workspaces, 4 fingers overview.
  • Tracking: 1:1 with the finger. The shape is the finger: no smoothing, no spring while the finger is down.
  • Limits: past a limit, rubber band: offset = (1 - 1 / (x x 0.55 / D + 1)) x D, D = the dimension on that axis.
  • Velocity: from the last 100 ms of samples (least squares), not the last delta.
  • Projection: end = position + v x 0.998 / (1 - 0.998) / 1000 (v in px/s). Snap to the nearest target to the projected end. Then settle on page with the finger's velocity as the start velocity.
  • Thresholds: a sheet opens if the projected end passes 50 % of its travel or v > 300 px/s toward open.
  • Cancel: a leave or cancel event settles to the snap target nearest the current position.

7.8 Reduced motion

Spatial motion becomes a crossfade on fade (in) and fade_out (out). The lens jumps and its new place fades in. No bounce, no scale, no slide, no stagger. Gestures still track the finger 1:1; release settles on close (no velocity carry, no overshoot). With animations off, every change is instant.

7.9 Implementation

  • Step springs on the frame clock (wl_surface.frame / presentation time), with the analytic solution re-seeded at each retarget. Never a wall-clock timer. Clamp dt to 50 ms after a stall.
  • Lay out once at the final size; animate transform, clip and radius in the renderer; relayout and resize the buffer once at the end.
  • Budget: per-frame work of an animating shell surface under 2 ms at 1.5 scale; no animation drops below the output refresh rate in a 60 fps or 120 fps recording.

7.10 Sources

Every value above was checked against these primary sources (2026-11-02). Where none of them settles a value, the row says so.

Rule Source What it says Here
spring form Apple, Animate with springs (WWDC23) duration = perceptual duration; stiffness = (2 pi / duration)^2; damping from bounce; mass 1 k = (2 pi / d)^2, z = 1 - b (7.2)
how much bounce same bounce 0 is the default; ~0.15 "doesn't feel very bouncy"; ~0.30 noticeable; be cautious above ~0.4 every bounce <= 0.25; frequent controls (snap) 0.15
bounce where momentum arrives Apple, Designing Fluid Interfaces (WWDC18) start tuning at 100 % damping; reward momentum with a little overshoot (Music dismiss: 80 % damping) rule 7.1.3; open 0.78, morph 0.75
retarget keeps velocity WWDC23 springs; WWDC18 a retargeted spring uses its current velocity; fully redirectable interface rule 7.1.5
gesture velocity, projection WWDC18 1:1 tracking; project the end point with the deceleration rate; rubber-band at limits 7.7 (rate 0.998 = UIScrollView normal)
do not wait for settling WWDC23 springs settling duration is unpredictable; follow-ups use perceptual completion gates on progress (7.1.6), never on settle
effects never overshoot Material 3, androidx ExpressiveMotionTokens / StandardMotionTokens effects springs damping 1.0, stiffness 1600 (default) / 3800 (fast) fade 1542, fade_out 3948 (7.2)
spatial spring range same expressive spatial: 380 / 0.8 (default), 800 / 0.6 (fast), 200 / 0.8 (slow); standard: 700 / 0.9, 1400 / 0.9, 300 / 0.9 open 224 / 0.78 = expressive slow; move 322 / 0.9 and collapse 386 / 0.9 = standard band
frequent interactions stay quiet Apple HIG Motion avoid adding motion to frequent interactions; brief and precise feedback; let people cancel motion snap and release lowered to 0.15 / 0.25; input never waits (7.1.8)
morph recipe no primary source: Apple does not publish Dynamic Island parameters. Recreations (sinasamaki, smoothui) use a spring on size, a short scale + blur crossfade on content, a firmer spring to collapse morph 0.46 / 0.25, collapse 0.32 / 0.10, faces 0.92 + blur 8 (7.4) are our choice; tune by side-by-side recording
content fade inside a moving shape Material MaterialContainerTransform.ProgressThresholds content fades over a sub-range of the shape's progress 35 % gate (7.4)

7.6 P10 · P11 · P12 · P15 · P16

Menus, dialogs, pages, windows

P10 Menu from its button · P12 Pages

The menu grows from the button corner (or the pointer: right-click the area). The current item is the lens. Drag the pages: 1:1, rubber band at the ends, release projects and settles on page with your velocity.

P15 Window from its dock icon · P16 minimize, close · P11 dialog

Click a dock icon: the window grows out of it. Minimize returns into the icon; close shrinks to 0.96 and fades. "Delete" opens an alert from the button.

8. Layout and composition

  • Bar: islands 32 high at the chrome gap (8) from the screen edge. Windows start at 8 + 32 + 8 = 48 from that edge.
  • Islands: left (app + workspaces), center (rest pill, morphs), right (status + clock). Each island is its own glass capsule; no full-width bar.
  • Sheets under islands: 8 below the island, aligned to the island's outer edge (right sheet: right edges equal).
  • Dock: 8 from the bottom edge, centred. Windows end 8 above it when it is not set to hide.
  • Tiling: 8 between windows and between a window and the screen, bar or dock. Maximize keeps the 8 gaps and the radius; fullscreen removes both.
  • Window content: page padding 24; content column max 640 for forms and Settings pages, centred; group gap 24.

10. Icons and cursors

  • Symbols: Tabler outline (shipped, noctalia-tabler.ttf), 24 grid, stroke 2, round caps and joins. Sizes per §2.1. The filled variant shows only an on-state. Colour: label_1 in controls, label_2 when secondary, accent_text only in the lens or an on-state.
  • App icons: from the icon theme, never masked or re-shaped; sizes per §2.1; a contact shadow E1 under icons of 48 or more on glass.
  • Cursors: one theme, size 24 x ui_scale. Arrow on every control; the hand only on text links. I-beam in text, resize cursors on window edges, grab / grabbing on drag handles. Busy (arrow + spinner) from an app launch until its window maps or 5 s pass.

11. Accessibility and focus

  • Focus ring: 2 px accent, 2 px gap, concentric outward (R7). Shown only after keyboard input; hidden on pointer use. One ring on screen at a time.
  • Keyboard: Tab moves between groups, arrows move inside a group (roving focus), Enter activates, Space toggles, Escape closes the topmost transient surface and returns focus to its source. Search is one key away: / in any list or Settings, Super for the launcher.
  • Increase contrast: label_2 to 80 %, label_3 to 56 %, stroke 0.5 -> 1 px at 24 %, glass -> thick (float) and solid (over), the lens gains a 1 px label_3 outline.
  • Reduce transparency: solid materials (§5.3). Reduce motion: §7.8.
  • Contrast floor: text 4.5:1 (label_1, label_2, accent_text on every plane; checked over glass by §5.3); symbols and control edges 3:1.
  • Screen readers: every control has a name and a role; the center island announces banners and live activity changes politely; Grow and Return move focus into and back out of the surface.

12. Density

Two densities for windows: Comfortable (default) and Compact. Compact steps every row down one size (40 -> 32, 56 -> 48), page padding 24 -> 16 and group gap 24 -> 16. Type, symbols, chrome (islands, dock, sheets, menus) do not change. Touch mode (§2.3) overrides both.

13. Sound

Sounds confirm events the user did not watch happen. Never for hover, navigation, toggles or anything already visible. freedesktop sound names; each under 500 ms (except ringtones); peak -12 dBFS; alert volume, muted by Focus.

Event Sound name
notification banner message-new-instant
incoming call phone-incoming-call (loops)
volume key audio-volume-change, once on key release
screenshot screen-capture
device plugged / unplugged device-added / device-removed
battery low (10 %, 5 %) battery-low
blocked action bell (only when no visible feedback is possible)

14. Writing

Sentence case. Labels name the thing ("Wi-Fi"), buttons say the verb ("Connect"). No full stop in labels; full stops in sentences. Status words are short and current ("On", "Off", "2 devices", "Charging"). Ellipsis only on a command that asks for more input ("Rename..."). Numbers as digits; percent without a space ("40%"), other units with one ("4.2 MB", "5 min").

15. Review checklist

  1. Every value in the change is in a scale (§2.1) or named by a rule (R1-R9).
  2. Every radius at a padding edge is concentric (R7); capsules stay capsules.
  3. Accent appears only on on-states, the focus ring and the lens symbol.
  4. Selection is the lens; hover is a fill ladder step.
  5. Every transition is one of the six verbs, on the named springs; it retargets; exits do not stagger.
  6. The surface opens from and returns to its source.
  7. Reduced motion, reduce transparency, increase contrast, light and dark were captured.
  8. A capture next to rulebook.html matches within 1 px at scale 1 and 1.5.

Deviations from the rulebook

Measured against docs/design/rulebook.md. Sources: protocol/design-tokens.toml, libdesk-ui/src/ui/style.h, shell/src/shell/*. Migration fixes the token file first; most surfaces then follow without code changes.

0. Size of the problem

  • Hard-coded size literals (<n>F) in shell/src/shell: about 5,300. About 240 are off the 4 grid (not a multiple of 4, between 2 and 400). Worst: lockscreen 51, bar 43, desktop 43, control_center 33, settings 27, live_activity 26.
  • Duration and easing animations (animFast/Normal/Slow, Easing::, EaseIn/Out): 211 uses in 59 files. Rule 7.1.1 allows springs only. Most: bar 18, lockscreen 11, control_center 10, notification 5, panel 4.
  • Rule 2.2 R1-R9 has no code form yet: nothing stops a new literal. Migration adds a check (step M5 below).

1. Tokens (protocol/design-tokens.toml)

4. Migration order (proposal)

  • M1 tokens. Rewrite protocol/design-tokens.toml to the rulebook: scales, type with tracking, colour roles with fill ladder and lens, E1-E4, the 12 springs. style.h aliases become scale names. Generated CSS, GTK, Qt and fcitx5 follow. Golden tests update.
  • M2 motion core. Shell animation API: springs only (animate(prop, target, Spring::Open)), progress gates, stagger helper, retarget with velocity, reduced-motion mapping (7.8). Remove duration APIs from shell surfaces.
  • M3 new components to spec. Bar islands, center island, sheet, dock to sections 9.1-9.4; side-by-side capture with rulebook.html#still crops at scale 1 and 1.5, light and dark.
  • M4 old surfaces. In this order: menus and tooltips (shared widgets), notifications + OSD (into the island), launcher, Settings S1 styling, dialogs, lock screen, switcher / overview / session (each needs an anatomy table first).
  • M5 guard. A lint in the shell build: no float size literal outside the token header and a short allow list; no duration animation outside continuous loops.

Open decisions for the user are listed in .agent/NEXT.md ("Rulebook").
